rv.q: There’s still a fundamental hollowness to the writing.
Though his writing aims for savagery, this trio – previously staged in the US – leave little more than a faint mark.
It isn't an uplifting evening's entertainment, but it is extremely well executed.
Confident performances deliver a clear production of the three half-hour plays, but the characters lack depth, and the storylines are slight.
Characters who operate at this level of ineptitude are very hard to sympathise with.

cn.t: LaBute's bleak triptych of American relationships divides critics with its cynical misanthropy. While some find merit in the provocative premise, most consider the unsympathetic characters and lack of remorse more sour than risky.
